Grip giving out before your back does is common, and it's a training problem we can work on. Here's what I'd do.

Add a dead hang or two at the end of your pull-up day, building up how long you can hold. Squeeze the bar hard from the start of each rep instead of loosening on the way down. Keep rows and heavy carries in your week too, since they load your grip without the swinging. Chalk helps if your gym allows it, and straps are fine on some back-focused sets, as long as your bare grip still gets its own work.

If you ever get pain or tingling in your hands or forearms, rather than plain tiredness, that one is for a doctor or physio.

If you want, I can look at how pull-ups are sitting in your program and add some grip work to it.
